checks: For b<1 the fixed-step image is the cap x_j≥b with constant density (1−b)^(−(m−1)); b=1 has zero probability under the density hypothesis. Integration and uniform averaging give the stated sum of integrals on the simplex interior.

The weight factor in the integral is bounded on every compact subinterval below 1, so G is absolutely continuous there. Full interior support and continuity give the stationarity identity at all interior points and at boundary tuples with no coordinate equal to 1, without any assumption about G(1).

For m≥3 both comparison tuples fit and avoid coordinates equal to 1. Canceling their common 1−x−y term gives additivity for x+y<1; G(0)=0 handles zeros. The centroid gives G(1/m)=1, so additivity fixes each rational grid k/(mn) below 1. These points are dense and continuity implies G(u)=mu.

Differentiating on compact subintervals and taking a countable exhaustion gives w(b)=m(1−b)^(m−1) almost everywhere. The beta-step predecessor proves sufficiency under the same independence assumptions.

The zero step gives the identity, so independent mixtures of it with the beta step preserve uniformity by linearity. For m=2 the deterministic half-step has two equal-volume images of density two before mixing, so the mixture is uniform. The draft makes no uniqueness assertion among arbitrary step laws.

The frozen source digest matches c6aadce19d219a98 at base 3220f79; §5 provides the density uniqueness and examples. The normalized proof makes the extension below 1 and the dense-grid argument explicit.

summary: For independent absolutely continuous steps in at least three barycentric coordinates, stationarity forces exactly the stated beta density. The two stationary examples outside those hypotheses are valid.
